solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Nut wrap and big cheese strip (8)

blocks.note: the head of an organisation is its big cheese
a band is a strip of material

annotation.surface: A deli order: a nut-filled wrap and a long strip of fancy cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like food, but 'nut' is slang for the head, so a 'nut wrap' is something wound round your head.
annotation.definitionFit: A headband is literally a wrap for the nut, slang for the head.

entries.clue: President touring old place where bills have gone up (8)

annotation.definition: place where bills have gone up

indicatorNotes.touring: the president travels round the old, so HARDING goes around O

blocks.note: Warren Harding, 29th US president
O is a standard abbreviation for old

annotation.surface: A president tours a historic venue where costs have risen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bills' look like invoices that have gone up in price; they are posters stuck up on a board. A hoarding is the British word for a billboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A hoarding is a large board on which bills (posters) are pasted up.

entries.clue: A hit getting sent up has tenor in bits (5)

indicatorNotes.sent up: in a down clue, sending a word up turns it round

blocks.note: taken as it stands
a rap is a sharp knock; turned round to PAR
T is the standard abbreviation for tenor

annotation.surface: A hit song is mocked, leaving the tenor's performance in pieces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit' reads as a chart song, and 'sent up' as mockery; here a hit is a rap, written upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a thing that has fallen apart lies in pieces.

entries.clue: Writing group in boat teenager upset (4,10)

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, rearranged

annotation.surface: A teenager is upset while sitting in a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The Beat Generation was the 1950s American literary movement of Kerouac and Ginsberg.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Kerouac, Ginsberg and Burroughs formed a literary circle in postwar America.

entries.clue: Bottle of note: present to customer unopened (5)

indicatorNotes.unopened: the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for note
to serve is to present something to a customer; minus its S it is ERVE

annotation.surface: A notable bottle of wine is handed to a customer still sealed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, not a wine bottle.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang, bottle is nerve or courage.

entries.clue: Switching starter, eat half of course? (4)

indicatorNotes.Switching starter: the first letter of the word is changed for another

blocks.note: to dine is to eat; its D is switched to N

annotation.surface: A diner swaps the starter and eats only half of the course.
annotation.walkthrough: The course is a golf course, not a meal: eighteen holes, so half is nine. The clue does not say which letter comes in; the definition settles it.
annotation.definitionFit: A full golf round has eighteen holes, so nine is half a course.

entries.clue: Why one might buy their eggs over the hill? (2,7)

annotation.definition: Why one might buy their eggs over the hill?

blocks.clueFragment: Why one might buy their eggs
blocks.note: the literal reading: with no hen of your own, you have to buy eggs
the real sense: old, past one's youth

annotation.surface: Someone goes to a shop beyond the hill to buy eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over the hill' seems to be where the shop is; it means old. 'No chicken', short for 'no spring chicken', describes someone past their youth.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who is no chicken is no longer young: over the hill.

entries.clue: Books covered in commendable literary review (6)

indicatorNotes.covered in: the books sit inside the other word, which wraps round them

blocks.note: nice = pleasing, worth commending
OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: Books are wrapped in praise in a literary review.
annotation.walkthrough: OT, the Old Testament, is a standard crossword source for 'books'.
annotation.definitionFit: A notice is a short review of a book or play in a newspaper.

entries.clue: Hear ignoble men started up Apple (8,6)

indicatorNotes.started up: the letters are stirred into action and rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, rearranged

annotation.surface: Word goes round that dishonourable men founded the Apple company.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital A makes 'Apple' look like the tech firm; it is the fruit. Blenheim Orange is an old English apple variety.
annotation.definitionFit: Blenheim Orange is a traditional English apple variety.

entries.clue: Turned fruit bishop brought to a relative (6)

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as it stands
nana is a grandmother

annotation.surface: A bishop brings some spoiled fruit to a relative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned' suggests fruit gone off; here it describes the banana's curved shape.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by shape: the familiar yellow fruit grows in a curve, as if turned.

entries.clue: Rook must get to King’s file: find move (8)

blocks.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
in chess the king starts on the e-file
to locate is to find

annotation.surface: A chess player plans to swing a rook over to the king's file.
annotation.walkthrough: The chess picture is kept up throughout: files are the board's columns, lettered a to h, and the king begins on e1.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: shifting home or office to a new place.

entries.clue: Something that comes in turns for Reform? (4)

indicatorNotes.turns: something that turns faces the other way, so the word is read back to front

blocks.note: the tide comes in and goes out

annotation.surface: A politician takes turns speaking for the Reform party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turns' first reads with 'comes in' as taking turns; it is the instruction to turn TIDE round. Reform UK is a British political party, hence the capital R.
annotation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to reshape and improve it.

entries.clue: Jealous creep entertaining female high-flyer (10)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: the host words take the female in as a guest

blocks.note: green with envy
to inch is to creep along
F is the standard abbreviation for female

annotation.surface: An envious sneak chats up an ambitious woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Creep' is a verb, not a person, and 'high-flyer' is literal: a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: The greenfinch is a common songbird, so a flyer in the sky.

entries.clue: Anger with necktie getting tangled up in tongue (7,5)

indicatorNotes.getting tangled up: the letters are knotted together and rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone fumes as their necktie gets tangled up, tongue and all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' means language, not the thing in your mouth.
annotation.definitionFit: Ancient Greek is the language of Homer and Plato.

entries.clue: Local manager hot to get new and handy footballer? (9)

blocks.note: hot = fashionable, in
N is the standard abbreviation for new
the goalkeeper is the one footballer allowed to use his hands

annotation.surface: A local football manager wants a new, useful player.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for your neighbourhood pub, so its manager runs the inn. 'Handy' means using the hands, not merely useful.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Britain your local is the nearby pub, and the person running an inn manages it.

entries.clue: Sentimentality is fine (most of the time) (3)

indicatorNotes.most of the time: most of the word is used, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: a four-letter word for fine or satisfactory; its last letter comes off

annotation.surface: A little sentimentality is acceptable, as long as it is not constant.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a mild caveat on the surface; it tells you to take most of GOOD.
annotation.definitionFit: Goo is sickly sentimentality, like gushing talk.

entries.clue: Desirable quality found in Essex housing essentially (8)

indicatorNotes.found: to found metal is to melt and cast it, so the letters are melted down and recast
indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence, or central letter, of the word

blocks.note: part of the fodder
the middle letter of HOUSING

annotation.surface: A desirable quality is discovered in housing in Essex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as 'discovered'; it is the foundry verb, to cast. 'Housing' looks like a container, but only its middle S is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: physical allure, the quality that makes a person attractive to others.

entries.clue: Modern ward in Barking with restricted views (6-6)

indicatorNotes.Barking: barking = mad, so the letters go crazy

blocks.note: the fodder, rearranged

annotation.surface: A new hospital ward in Barking has poor windows.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, so it looks like a place name; 'barking' is also British slang for mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A narrow-minded person has restricted views, closed to other opinions.

entries.clue: A daughter opening something prior to Christmas? (6)

blocks.note: taken as it stands
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a vent is an opening

annotation.surface: A daughter opens a present early, before Christmas Day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the verb from present-opening; it is a noun, a vent.
annotation.definitionFit: Advent is the season of the four weeks before Christmas.

entries.clue: Risk-taker seen in rare nude TV broadcast (10)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: the letters are scattered widely and rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, rearranged

annotation.surface: A daring performer appears naked on a rare television broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the TV picture so well it passes for part of the story, but it is the instruction to scatter the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An adventurer takes risks in search of excitement or gain.

entries.clue: Apparatus tackling, primarily, nuisance calls (5)

indicatorNotes.tackling: the gear gets to grips with the letter, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.primarily: only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: rigs are sets of equipment; apparatus can be plural
the first letter of nuisance

annotation.surface: A device deals with unwanted nuisance phone calls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nuisance calls' looks like one phrase, but only the N of nuisance is used and 'calls' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to call them, so rings are calls.

entries.clue: Killer from close to Cincinnati in US jail (4)

indicatorNotes.close to: only the closing letter of the next word is used
indicatorNotes.in: that letter goes inside the jail

blocks.note: can is American slang for prison
the last letter of Cincinnati

annotation.surface: A murderer from near Cincinnati is locked up in an American prison.
annotation.walkthrough: Cain is the Bible's first murderer, who killed his brother Abel.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in Genesis the first murderer slew his brother Abel.

entries.clue: Get in trouble being sanctimonious in bed (3,2)

indicatorNotes.in: the sanctimonious word lies inside the bed

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
pi is slang for pious

annotation.surface: Someone is scolded for being holier-than-thou in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cop it' is British slang for being punished or getting into trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: British slang for being caught and punished.

entries.clue: Blue upon blue in your heart of hearts (4,4)

blocks.note: the deep is the sea, the blue
blue = sad, down

annotation.surface: Feeling blue upon blue, sad to the very core.
annotation.walkthrough: The two blues are different: the first is the sea, 'the deep', and the second is a low mood.
annotation.definitionFit: Deep down means in your innermost feelings, your heart of hearts.

entries.clue: Dozy type of kid making one amused … initially (6)

indicatorNotes.making: the one is made into something else, so I is swapped out
indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of amused is used

blocks.note: a nipper is a small child
I is the Roman numeral one; it comes out
the first letter of amused; it goes in

annotation.surface: A sleepy child makes someone smile at first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' is part of the machinery, not the definition: the definition is 'Dozy type', and NIPPER turns I into A.
annotation.definitionFit: A napper is someone who naps, a dozy type.

entries.clue: Sulphur, bitumen-like substance and lead (4)

blocks.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
tar is a black sticky substance like bitumen

annotation.surface: A list of chemical ingredients: sulphur, tar and lead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal in a list of chemicals; it is the lead role, the star.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the theatre: the principal performer takes the leading role.

entries.clue: Dope, elite officer at front admitted, is toxic stuff (8)

indicatorNotes.at front: only the front letter of officer is used
indicatorNotes.admitted: the letters are let into the dope

blocks.note: an ass is a fool, a dope
the elite are the best
the first letter of officer

annotation.surface: A top officer admits taking drugs and poisonous substances.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' reads as drugs; it is a fool, an ass, which opens to take in the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral whose dust is toxic when breathed in.
